newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tsumura adopts new restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Tsumura adopts new restructuring plan.

text.p: Tsumura & Co, a top Japanese manufacturer of herbal medicines, unveiled on Thursday a new restructuring programme covering the three years to March 31, 2000 that aims to boost sales and cut costs and debt.
The new programme is a revised version of a restructuring plan covering the three-year period to March 31, 1999, the company said in a statement.
"We have been trying to proceed with the (old) programme, but as sales of herbal medicines have fallen, we now expect a sharp fall in profits (in 1996/97)," the company said.
Under the new programme, Tsumura will aim at 100 billion yen in sales in 1999/2000 through various marketing activities and the introduction of new products, the company said.
Tsumura also said that, under the new programme, it would try to cut its debt by more than 20 billion yen from over 130 billion yen currently.
It will also aim to reduce its workforce to fewer than 2,900 employees by the end of March 2000 from about 3,370 workers at the end of September 1996, by not recruiting new workers.
Tsumura also said it will squeeze capital spending and cut inventories of materials for medicines, while seeking to cut other costs as well.
Tsumura hopes its cosmetics unit will return to profitability on an operating basis in 1997/98 and will try to proceed with further restructuring of other units.
Earlier on Thursday, Tsumura said that it lowered its parent current profit forecast for 1996/97 to 3.2 billion yen from its previous forecast of 6.0 billion yen.
It also projected a parent net loss of 2.1 billion yen in 1996/97, against its earlier forecast of a net profit of 3.6 billion yen.

The expected net loss was due to an extraordinary loss of 9.1 billion yen partly stemming from the liquidation of subsidiaries, Tsumura said. Its 1996/97 earnings will also include an extraordinary profit of 4.3 billion yen mainly from securities sales, it said.
